title: Image Segmentation Quiz
description: Test your understanding of image segmentation

questions.question: What is the main difference between image classification and image segmentation?
options: Classification is faster than segmentation
Classification assigns one label to the entire image, while segmentation classifies every pixel
Segmentation only works on grayscale images
Classification requires more training data
questions.explanation: Image classification assigns a single label to an entire image, while segmentation provides pixel-level understanding by classifying each pixel individually. This allows segmentation to identify where objects are located and their precise boundaries.

questions.question: What type of segmentation assigns a class label to every pixel without distinguishing between different instances of the same class?
options: Instance segmentation
Panoptic segmentation
Semantic segmentation
Binary segmentation
questions.explanation: Semantic segmentation assigns a class label to every pixel (e.g., 'car', 'road', 'sky') but doesn't distinguish between different instances of the same class. All cars would be labeled as 'car' without individual identification.

questions.question: Why do we include position features (x, y coordinates) in addition to color features for image segmentation?
options: To make the algorithm run faster
To create spatially coherent segments where nearby similar pixels are grouped together
To reduce the number of segments needed
To improve color accuracy
questions.explanation: Position features help create spatially coherent segments by encouraging nearby pixels with similar colors to be grouped together. This reduces fragmentation and produces more meaningful, connected regions rather than scattered pixels of the same color.

questions.question: What does the position weight parameter control in image segmentation?
options: The total number of segments
The balance between color similarity and spatial proximity
The speed of the algorithm
The image resolution
questions.explanation: The position weight controls the trade-off between grouping pixels by color similarity versus spatial proximity. Higher weights create more spatially compact segments, while lower weights prioritize color similarity regardless of location.

questions.question: What is the purpose of k-means++ initialization in segmentation?
options: To reduce the number of iterations needed
To choose initial cluster centers that are well-spread, improving convergence and quality
To automatically determine the optimal number of segments
To normalize the pixel features
questions.explanation: K-means++ initialization strategically selects initial cluster centers that are far apart from each other. This leads to better convergence, faster training, and higher quality segmentation compared to random initialization.

questions.question: What does the inertia metric measure in image segmentation?
options: The number of segments in the image
The sum of squared distances from pixels to their cluster centers
The accuracy of the segmentation
The time taken to segment the image
questions.explanation: Inertia measures the sum of squared distances from each pixel to its assigned cluster center. Lower inertia indicates tighter, more compact clusters. However, inertia always decreases with more segments, so it should be combined with other evaluation criteria.

questions.question: What happens when you use only color features (no position features) for segmentation?
options: The algorithm fails to converge
Pixels with similar colors are grouped together regardless of their location, potentially creating fragmented segments
The segmentation becomes more accurate
The number of segments automatically increases
questions.explanation: Using only color features groups pixels based solely on appearance similarity, regardless of where they are in the image. This can create fragmented segments where spatially separated regions of similar color are grouped together, lacking spatial coherence.

questions.question: In the k-means segmentation algorithm, what happens during the assignment step?
options: New cluster centers are computed
Each pixel is assigned to the nearest cluster center based on feature distance
The number of segments is determined
Features are normalized
questions.explanation: During the assignment step, each pixel is assigned to the cluster whose center is closest to the pixel's feature vector. This is done by computing the distance between the pixel's features and each cluster center, then choosing the minimum.

questions.question: What is a major limitation of clustering-based segmentation compared to deep learning approaches?
options: It's too slow for practical use
It requires more training data
It lacks semantic understanding and relies only on low-level features
It can only segment grayscale images
questions.explanation: Clustering-based segmentation groups pixels based on low-level features (color, position) without understanding what objects actually are. Deep learning approaches can learn semantic understanding, recognizing 'car' or 'person' rather than just 'similar-colored region'.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical application of image segmentation?
options: Medical imaging for tumor detection
Autonomous vehicle road scene understanding
Predicting future frames in a video
Background removal in photo editing
questions.explanation: Predicting future video frames is a temporal prediction task, not segmentation. Image segmentation applications include medical imaging (tumor detection), autonomous vehicles (scene understanding), and photo editing (background removal) - all involving partitioning images into regions.
